_notes: PreToolUse guard on Write: a file under a `drafts/` path component must have a matching
outline in the sibling `outlines/` directory, or the tool call is DENIED via _gate_common.deny
(stdout JSON, permissionDecision 'deny', exit 0). Every non-deny branch is silence + exit 0,
so the cases below are distinguished by WHICH early return they take, not by their output.
All file_paths are RELATIVE on purpose: the deny message embeds `file_path`, `outlines_dir`
and the derived section name verbatim. An absolute path would bake a temp-dir name into the
expected stdout. Relative paths keep the deny text identical for both implementations.
Branch map (source line refs are to hooks/writing-outline-guard.py at the port base):
section name empties out     -> exit 0             (case: allow-unnameable-section)
outlines/ exists, no match   -> deny               (case: deny-outline-missing-sibling-dir)
The 'unparseable stdin' case omits `stdin` entirely — the harness then runs the hook with
stdin 'ignore', so json.load hits EOF and raises, which is exactly the caught branch.
No branch of this hook writes anything, so every case's expected filesystem delta is empty.
